item: Al family band tape, 12 mm bands (blue)
pack: 1 roll, 1/2 in x 108 ft (36 yd), 0.006 in
qty_basis: brief: 2 rolls per colour at 1/2 in
notes: Target #0072B2. 471 Blue is a mid 'safety' blue; closeness not measured. 3M 471 is PVC film with rubber adhesive, rated 40-170 F (4-77 C) on both the McMaster and Uline pages; Uline: 'maintains color even with heavy abrasion', 'residue-free removal', not for outdoor use. Fine for hand washing and isopropanol wipes (test IPA on a cut edge first: solvent can soften the rubber adhesive), but NOT rated for an autoclave (121-134 C) or a washer-disinfector's thermal stage (about 90 C). 3M publishes no sRGB value; measure the roll before re-running the colour-vision check. McMaster page shows no stock line.

item: Powder-waste can per family, closable bare steel, 1 gal (gets a 25 mm family band)
pack: 1 carton of 34 unlined tin-plated steel 1 gal paint cans with lids
qty_basis: 2 families + 1 spare = 3 cans; Uline sells only by the carton of 34, so full cans can be sealed and sent out as waste in the can and replaced

alt.part_no: 4173T16 300-series stainless batch can, 2 gal + 4173T26 loose-fitting lid

notes: Bare tin-plated steel (neutral, unpainted), noncombustible. Uline: 'suitable for hazardous materials; unlined; lids included'. It is leakproof with the separate S-8249 clips, and a rubber mallet closes the lid. The friction lid seals tightly but is slow to open, so for a can opened daily the stainless alt ($48.61 can + $18.20 lid, reusable but loose-lidded) suits better. McMaster's 2 gal galvanized pail 4260T1 ($14.98) shows no lid. No fetched page stated what NFPA 484/660 requires of a fines container. Confirm it with BYU EHS, along with disposal. Never put Al and Cu fines in the same can (thermite).

item: Pocket colour sensor to measure the bought colours, optional
notes: Gives RGB/HEX/CMYK readings through the Nix Toolkit app; IPX4, 2-year warranty, made in Canada (page). Paint-matching grade; no accuracy figure was read. If the CAM02-UCS check needs better accuracy, look at Nix's Spectro line (not priced). Read the tapes on the tool itself, because thin vinyl over steel reads differently from vinyl on white.
